LQG controller

Source: R/estimation.R
ctrl_lqg.Rd

Combine an LQR state feedback with a steady-state Kalman filter. Under the separation principle (linear model, Gaussian noise with the given covariances, and stabilizing LQR and Kalman designs) the closed-loop poles are the union of the regulator poles, eig(A - BK), and the estimator poles, eig(A - LC). LQG controllers have no guaranteed robustness margins (Doyle, 1978); check margins of the actual loop.

Usage

ctrl_lqg(
  sys,
  Q,
  R,
  Qn,
  Rn,
  N = NULL,
  Nn = NULL,
  G = NULL,
  form = c("current", "delayed")
)

Arguments

sys

Plant model.

Q, R, N

LQR weights (see ctrl_lqr()).

Qn, Rn, Nn, G

Noise model (see ctrl_kalman()).

form

"current" or "delayed" (discrete models only).

Value

An object of class c("ctrl_lqg", "ctrl_controller") with controller (a ctrl_ss model from y to u), lqr, kalman and form.

Details

The controller maps measurements y to inputs u (it contains the minus sign of the feedback):

  • continuous time and discrete form = "delayed": \(\dot{\hat x} = (A - BK - LC + LDK)\hat x + L y\), \(u = -K\hat x\);

  • discrete form = "current": the input uses the measurement-updated estimate \(\hat x_{k|k}\), \(u_k = -K \hat x_{k|k}\), which reacts to \(y_k\) without a one-sample delay.

References

Doyle, J. C. (1978). Guaranteed margins for LQG regulators. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, 23(4), 756-757.

Examples

plant <- ctrl_c2d(ctrl_ss(matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0, 1),
                          c(1, 0)), 0.1)
lqg <- ctrl_lqg(plant, Q = diag(c(1, 0.1)), R = 0.1, Qn = diag(c(1e-4, 1e-3)),
                Rn = 1e-2)
cl <- ctrl_closed_loop(plant, lqg)
ctrl_poles(cl)
#> [1] 0.8677171+0.1006218i 0.8677171-0.1006218i 0.8675449+0.1003633i
#> [4] 0.8675449-0.1003633i
